extracted.intended_audience: general readers and journalists interested in academic misconduct and Hungarian politics
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing alleged plagiarism, multiple submission, and procedural irregularities in university theses and degree-conversion processes, as discussed in a high-profile Hungarian political case. The page summarizes alleged violations, institutional responses, and relevant higher-education rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism: unattributed use of external sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Material has been taken from various sources without proper citation (e.g., 'material that amounts to 40 percent' of the 1991 dissertation was taken from various sources without proper citation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page gives examples (verbatim copying, omitted words, synonym replacement, reversed word order) and identifies specific external sources (Üblackner, von Glasenapp, Spence, Gassmann). Notes that some verbatim quotations were referenced correctly (about 25%), while other material was not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-plagiarism / multiple submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of overlapping material to two separate theses (1991 laureatus dissertation and 1992 sociology diploma thesis) without indicating prior submission or bibliographic acknowledgement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HVG identified 32–33 overlapping pages out of 46 in the sociology thesis, including word-by-word copying in parts and slightly reformulated text in others. The page highlights failure to indicate prior submission in text or bibliography as an issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to use quotation marks and indicate origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Text that was properly cited in an earlier dissertation appears in a later thesis without quotation marks or indication of origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include material present in the 1991 dissertation with correct citations but appearing in the 1992 thesis stripped of quotation marks or origin notes. The absence of quotation marks is flagged as a specific form of improper attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism from supervisor or other authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections of the thesis are largely identical to publications by the thesis advisor (Attila Molnár) or other authors, raising questions of who appropriated whose text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HVG reported 12–13 pages in the revised 1992 thesis matching Molnár's 1993 Valóság article; ELTE investigation found overlap but did not investigate Molnár's role. The page records conflicting claims (Molnár denies taking from students; others point to identical passages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Original research and scientific contribution requirement for PhD
rubrics_metrics.description: PhD regulations require that a doctorate contain original research and results; a thesis that is mainly review/educational literature may not satisfy PhD standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Népszabadság argued Semjén's laureatus lacked original research and relied mainly on educational rather than scientific literature. The conversion to PhD should assess compliance with conditions and regulations in force at the time of conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documented scientific achievements requirement for degree conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversion of earlier doctorates to PhD required assessment of the candidate's publications and scientific work; 'subsequent scientific achievements' are decisive under the conversion process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page cites the Higher Education Act of 1993 and notes that conversions up to the end of 1997 were case-by-case and required examination of candidate's publications and scientific output. Dispute exists over whether Semjén met these criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign language examination requirement for PhD
rubrics_metrics.description: PhD regulations may require passing language examinations in two foreign languages as part of degree requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Népszabadság raised the claim that Semjén did not take and/or pass language examinations in two foreign languages, which would be required by PhD regulations; the issue remained unresolved as PPKE did not investigate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and legality of degree-conversion procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversion of a laureatus degree to a PhD must be carried out by an authorized committee in accordance with the Hungarian Accreditation Commission and relevant laws; questions may arise about who had authority to sign conversion documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Népszava questioned whether Péter Erdő, as dean, had authority to grant the conversion; PPKE/rector responded that an international committee dealt with conversions and that the university was authorized by MAB. The page stresses conversions were substantive case-by-case decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and statutory deadline for degree conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversions of previously awarded doctorates to PhD degrees were allowed up until a statutory deadline (end of 1997); conversions close to that deadline may be scrutinized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semjén's laureatus degree was converted in December 1997, just before the deadline; the page flags timing as relevant to scrutiny over procedural correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation scope and institutional jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional investigations must have clear scope and legal jurisdiction; some findings may be declared but institutions may state they are not in a position to take official action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ELTE's three-member committee concluded serious ethical, professional misconduct but said the university was not in a position to take official action; PPKE declined to investigate and considered the case closed. HVG criticized ELTE's investigation as incomplete for not addressing self-plagiarism, other-source plagiarism, and revision-submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer disagreement and review-procedure rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When thesis reviewers strongly disagree (one gives highest grade, another a failing grade), standard procedure is to bring in a third reviewer who evaluates the same submitted work; rules around rewriting/resubmitting instead of re-review can be controversial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page reports one reviewer gave 5/5, another 1/5 (arguing the work was theological not sociological); a third reviewer was invited and gave 4/5. HVG raised whether 1992 regulations allowed rewriting/resubmitting a thesis given a failing grade rather than the third reviewer assessing the originally submitted work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of evaluation documents and reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of the three reviews (and other internal documents) is important to answer procedural questions about assessment and whether revisions were permitted or reviewed correctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HVG noted the question about rewriting/resubmitting could be answered if Semjén released the three reviews; lack of transparency was cited as an investigative gap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical/professional standards and no statute of limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations of scientific ethics (e.g., plagiarism) are serious and 'have no term of limitation'; moral assessment does not necessarily require special regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twelve ELTE lecturers stated the significant identical text indicates a serious violation of scientific ethics, damaging the moral foundations of research and education; they asserted the case cannot be regarded as closed until clarification of responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervisor and examiner responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Supervisors and examiners have responsibility to warn students of problematic practices and to detect issues; possible culpability extends to supervisors if misconduct occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semjén claimed he acted in good faith and blamed lecturers for not warning him. ELTE professors condemned behavior and said responsibility could lie with the defending student, the supervisor, or both; the role of Molnár (advisor) was a specific focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of educational versus scientific source material
rubrics_metrics.description: A doctoral thesis should rely on scientific literature and produce new findings rather than primarily using educational or summary sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Népszabadság argued many of Semjén's sources fell into the category of educational rather than scientific literature, undermining the thesis's adequacy for PhD conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright/publication precedence as an argument in disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: In disputes over identical text, parties may cite copyright law principles (e.g., 'the one who publishes first has precedence').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KDNP representative Rubovszky invoked copyright precedence to argue Molnár should not be considered aggrieved because Semjén published first; the page records this as part of political/institutional reactions, not a settled adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of investigations: addressing self-plagiarism and multiple-source plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: A thorough inquiry should address self-plagiarism (reuse of one's own earlier work) and plagiarism from all other sources, not only specific identified authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HVG criticized the ELTE committee for failing to address self-plagiarism, plagiarism from authors other than Molnár, and regulations permitting submission of a revised thesis edition; HVG called the investigation incomplete for leaving these questions unresolved.
